opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Sloan (employee ID E043) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E043.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Karen Sloan is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted per policy. Recommend granting admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E043 (Karen Sloan) is a contractor with basic training, not full-time. Contractors max out at read without advanced training and never admin. Recommend granting read (the maximum for this contractor), not admin.
reason: There is a conflict between the two notes: HR claims Karen Sloan is a full-time Payroll Specialist (which would allow admin), while Security's database shows she is a contractor with basic training. Per policy, contractors may never have admin, and without advanced security training the maximum level for a contractor is read. Given the conflicting evidence, the conservative and policy-compliant decision is to grant read, the maximum permitted for a contractor with basic training. Requested admin exceeds this maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed level.
